original_question: Let G = SL(K), where K is an infinite field. Is the cardinal symmetry number MS_r^+(G) equal to |G|^+ for every finite number of colors r?
target_in_paper: Section 8, Problem 8.8: Let G = SL(K) for an infinite field K. Is MS_r^+(G) = |G|^+ for all finite cardinals r?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended target very closely: it identifies the same group G = SL(K), the hypothesis that K is an infinite field, the same successor-cardinal symmetry invariant MS_r^+(G), and the same quantifier over all finite numbers of colors r. In substance, it is essentially Problem 8.8.
missing_details: The paper's MS_r^+(G) is defined in Section 8 using the symmetry measure space (G, card^+, S), where card^+(A) = |A|^+ for every A ⊂ G.
The relevant admissible symmetries are the central symmetries S = {s_c : c ∈ G}, where s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c.
A 'symmetric subset' here means an S-symmetric subset A ⊂ G, i.e. A = s_c(A) for some c ∈ G; equivalently A = c A^{-1} c.
The paper phrases the color parameter as 'for all finite cardinals r', so that should be stated explicitly rather than only informally as a finite number of colors.
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should specify that the underlying measurable sets are all subsets of G, i.e. the full power set P(G).

Nearby context matters: Example 8.7 proves the case MS_2^+(SL(K)) = |G|^+ for infinite fields K of characteristic ≠ 2, and Problem 8.8 asks whether this persists for all finite r and arbitrary infinite fields K.
refined_question: Let K be an infinite field and let G = SL(K). View G as the symmetry measure space (G, card^+, S), where the underlying σ-algebra is P(G), card^+(A) = |A|^+ for A ⊂ G, and S = {s_c : c ∈ G} is the family of central symmetries s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c. Is it true that for every finite cardinal r, the cardinal symmetry number MS_r^+(G) = ms_r(G, card^+, S) is equal to |G|^+?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. Section 8 defines the invariants MS_r(G) and MS_r^+(G) for groups using central symmetries and the successor-cardinal measure. Example 8.7 then states that for any infinite field K of characteristic not equal to 2, G = SL(K) satisfies MS_2^+(G) = |G|^+, and Problem 8.8 asks exactly whether the same equality holds for all finite cardinals r when G = SL(K) for an infinite field K. Your draft captures that problem almost verbatim; the needed refinements are mainly the paper's built-in definitions of MS_r^+(G) and of 'symmetric subset'.
